The displayed 4c(c-e)n is correct only after substituting em = cn + (em-cn), i.e. 2c y_m = 2c y_0 + 2c^2 n + 2c(em-cn), so the residual is 2c(em-cn)+const = O(1) precisely along |cn-em|<1 (and =const in Case 1, using cq=ep). The write-up never performs this regrouping; it asserts \"+O(1)\" in Case 2 while (5) only guarantees O(n+m), which cannot be dominated by a linear negative term.
